answers.children: Dogo Argentinos are moderately good with children when raised with them. Their large muscular build from hunting large game in Argentina means a playful nudge can easily knock over a toddler while their protective loyalty makes them devoted once bonds form though their strength requires careful management around small kids. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Dogo Argentinos do not get along reliably with other pets. Their powerful prey drive bred for tracking and taking down wild boar and puma leads to intense chasing of smaller animals while same-sex tension can arise from the Cordoba Fighting Dog ancestry making multi-pet homes challenging without experienced handling.
answers.exercise: Dogo Argentinos need 90 minutes to two hours of vigorous exercise daily. Without it their high energy from hunting in rugged South American terrain turns into destructive behaviour such as tearing apart a backyard while activities like long hikes weight-pulling or running suit their muscular build and exceptional endurance.
answers.shedding: Yes — Dogo Argentinos shed moderately with no strong seasonal pattern. Their short smooth all-white coat from the hunting lines produces visible white hair on furniture and clothing yet the single-layer texture means it brushes off easily compared to longer or double coats.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Dogo Argentino has a short smooth coat that sheds lightly and produces minimal loose hair around the house. Its sleek white coat requires little grooming yet still spreads dander through normal activity. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Dogo Argentino is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers.
answers.training: Dogo Argentinos are not easy to train. Their stubborn nature combined with the courageous independence bred for pack hunting large game demands experienced handling and firm boundaries as their intelligence responds well only when the owner matches their protective drive with consistent leadership.
answers.lifespan: Dogo Argentinos live 10-15 years. Their health robustness ties to the muscular build refined over decades from crosses like the Great Dane and Boxer for hunting endurance in Argentina yet their powerful frame and protective intensity mean they thrive only with owners who provide the structured activity their history requires.
answers.size: Dogo Argentinos reach 80-100 lb and stand 24-27 in tall. The broad powerful proportions from their development as fearless hunters of wild boar create a rippling muscular presence that feels substantial indoors where their sheer mass and protective stance command space even when resting.
answers.barking: Dogo Argentinos do not bark a lot. Their quiet confidence and low barking score stem from the controlled drive refined for high-stakes hunts where they focus on tracking rather than alerting making them more likely to growl deeply at strangers than to vocalise frequently.
answers.apartment: Dogo Argentinos do not suit apartment living. Their high energy and protective streak from Argentine hunting ancestry make them restless indoors without room to move while their size and need for vigorous daily outlets lead to frustration in confined spaces with limited exercise options.
answers.first-time: Dogo Argentinos are not a good first dog. Their stubbornness and requirement for experienced handling to channel the courageous protective instincts from large-game hunting make them too demanding for novices who may struggle to establish the firm leadership their loyalty needs.
